notes: Profile: mid-to-large legal eDiscovery vendor. Heavy search + rerank workload; 180M doc corpus (emails, contracts, filings).
Current stack: BM25 + SBERT (sentence-transformers) reranker for top-50 hits. They pay external embedding vendor today; cost per query ~ $0.035 at 95th. Want to get under $0.02.
Primary drivers: reduce per-query cost, tighten p95 latency (<150ms end-to-end for search), and ensure no relevance regressions for Triage & Privilege review flows.

POC ask: run embeddings + new learned reranker (distilled cross-encoder) vs current SBERT reranker on 20k labeled holdout with DCG/NDCG, recall@k, and precision@k, plus human eval on 1k critical queries.

Evals plan: SE to provide harness that computes NDCG@10, pairwise win-rate, and failure cases. Lacuna insists on canary A/B with rollback automatically triggered if NDCG drops > 1.5 points or customer-reported misses > 0.5%.

Latency/infra: Target 120 qps sustained for top-k retrieval + rerank path during peak (legal big batch jobs). P95 overall response <= 150ms for interactive UI. Need quant and batching guidance from Redwood Optimize.
Indexing constraints: 180M docs -> average doc length 1.2k tokens. Concern about shard sizing and memory for KV caches. Asking about prefix caching + partial reranker offload to CPU for cost saving.
Security: must run in VPC/on-prem for regulated clients; KMS + audit logs mandatory. They will not accept hosted API for certain clients. Air-gapped option may be requested later.
Quote from CTO: 'We cannot tolerate subtle quality regressions—a 1% drop in relevance equals thousands in manual review costs.' Wants regression alarms tied to eval set and production A/B telemetry.
Competitor checks: evaluated Pinecone + OpenAI embeddings earlier; liked Pinecone's vector scale but worried about reranker integration and cost. Curious about Redwood's rollback + canary tooling.
Next deliverables: SE to deliver eval harness + baseline runs by 2024-11-08. AE to coordinate security call with compliance on 2024-11-05.
Notes on economics: asking for detailed cost model (embedding compute + reranker GPU vs quantized CPU reranker) and expected $/query sensitivity by QPS and hit rate.
